requirements.quote:
The SETTINGS frames received from a peer as part of the connection
   preface MUST be acknowledged (see Section 6.5.3) after sending the
   connection preface.
requirements.condition: A SETTINGS frame is received from a peer as part of the connection preface, and the local endpoint has sent its connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior: Acknowledge the received SETTINGS frame after sending the connection preface.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can observe whether and when the endpoint acknowledges the peer's connection-preface SETTINGS frame.

requirements.quote:
To avoid unnecessary latency, clients are permitted to send
   additional frames to the server immediately after sending the client
   connection preface, without waiting to receive the server connection
   preface.  It is important to note, however, that the server
requirements.condition: A client has sent the client connection preface but has not yet received the server connection preface.
requirements.required_behavior: The client is permitted to send additional frames immediately.
requirements.why_checkable: A client implementation can be tested for allowing frame transmission during the stated preface interval.

requirements.quote:
server.  Upon receiving the SETTINGS frame, the client is expected to
   honor any settings established.  In some configurations, it is
requirements.condition: A client receives the server's SETTINGS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Honor every setting established by the received SETTINGS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Subsequent client behavior can be checked against each setting established in the received frame.

requirements.quote:
Clients and servers MUST treat an invalid connection preface as a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.  A GOAWAY
requirements.condition: A client or server receives an invalid connection preface.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the invalid preface as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A malformed preface can be supplied and the resulting connection-level error type observed.

requirements.quote:
connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.  A GOAWAY
   frame (Section 6.8) MAY be omitted in this case, since an invalid
   preface indicates that the peer is not using HTTP/2.
requirements.condition: An invalid connection preface has been detected.
requirements.required_behavior: The endpoint is permitted to omit a GOAWAY frame.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can verify that omission of GOAWAY is accepted for this specific error case.

requirements.quote:
All frames begin with a fixed 9-octet header followed by a variable-
   length frame payload.
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 frame is encoded or parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent the frame as a fixed 9-octet header followed by a variable-length payload.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized layout and header length can be inspected directly.

requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 frame header is encoded or parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode Length as 24 bits followed by Type as 8 bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The field widths and ordering are directly inspectable in serialized frame bytes.

requirements.quote:
Type (8),

     Flags (8),
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 frame header is encoded or parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the 8-bit Flags field after the 8-bit Type field.
requirements.why_checkable: The field widths and ordering are directly inspectable in serialized frame bytes.

requirements.quote:
Reserved (1),
     Stream Identifier (31),
requirements.condition: An HTTP/2 frame header is encoded or parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode a 1-bit Reserved field followed by a 31-bit Stream Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The bit allocation can be checked in the serialized header.

requirements.quote:
Length:  The length of the frame payload expressed as an unsigned
      24-bit integer in units of octets.  Values greater than 2^14
      (16,384) MUST NOT be sent unless the receiver has set a larger
      value for SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a frame and the receiver has not set SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE above 16,384 octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send a frame payload whose Length value is greater than 16,384 octets.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frame lengths can be compared with the receiver's advertised maximum.

requirements.quote:
Length:  The length of the frame payload expressed as an unsigned
      24-bit integer in units of octets.  Values greater than 2^14
requirements.condition: A frame Length field is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Express the frame-payload length as an unsigned 24-bit integer measured in octets.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded width, unsigned interpretation, unit, and correspondence to payload size can be validated.

requirements.quote: The 9 octets of the frame header are not included in this value.
requirements.condition: A frame Length value is calculated or validated.
requirements.required_behavior: Exclude the 9-octet frame header from the Length value.
requirements.why_checkable: The Length field can be compared with payload size independently of the header.

requirements.quote:
Type:  The 8-bit type of the frame.  The frame type determines the
      format and semantics of the frame.  Frames defined in this
      document are listed in Section 6.  Implementations MUST ignore and
      discard frames of unknown types.
requirements.condition: An implementation receives a frame whose 8-bit Type value is unknown.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore and discard the frame.
requirements.why_checkable: An unknown frame type can be injected and the implementation's processing and state effects observed.

requirements.quote:
Flags are assigned semantics specific to the indicated frame type.
      Unused flags are those that have no defined semantics for a
      particular frame type.  Unused flags MUST be ignored on receipt
      and MUST be left unset (0x00) when sending.
requirements.condition: A received frame has flag bits with no defined semantics for its frame type.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the unused flag bits.
requirements.why_checkable: Unused received bits can be varied while checking that parsing and state remain unaffected.

requirements.quote:
Flags are assigned semantics specific to the indicated frame type.
      Unused flags are those that have no defined semantics for a
      particular frame type.  Unused flags MUST be ignored on receipt
      and MUST be left unset (0x00) when sending.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a frame with flag bits that have no defined semantics for that frame type.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave all unused flag bits unset at 0x00.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Set an unused flag bit when sending.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frame flag octets can be inspected for nonzero unused bits.

requirements.quote:
Reserved:  A reserved 1-bit field.  The semantics of this bit are
      undefined, and the bit MUST remain unset (0x00) when sending and
      MUST be ignored when receiving.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends an HTTP/2 frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the reserved header bit unset at 0x00.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Set the reserved header bit when sending.
requirements.why_checkable: The reserved bit is directly inspectable in every outbound frame header.

requirements.quote:
Reserved:  A reserved 1-bit field.  The semantics of this bit are
      undefined, and the bit MUST remain unset (0x00) when sending and
      MUST be ignored when receiving.
requirements.condition: An endpoint receives an HTTP/2 frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the reserved header bit.
requirements.why_checkable: Frames with the reserved bit set can be injected and checked for unchanged interpretation apart from that bit.

requirements.quote:
Stream Identifier:  A stream identifier (see Section 5.1.1) expressed
      as an unsigned 31-bit integer.  The value 0x00 is reserved for
      frames that are associated with the connection as a whole as
      opposed to an individual stream.
requirements.condition: A frame Stream Identifier is encoded or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Express the stream identifier as an unsigned 31-bit integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The field's width and unsigned interpretation can be checked in the frame header.

requirements.quote:
Stream Identifier:  A stream identifier (see Section 5.1.1) expressed
      as an unsigned 31-bit integer.  The value 0x00 is reserved for
      frames that are associated with the connection as a whole as
      opposed to an individual stream.
requirements.condition: A frame is associated with the connection as a whole rather than an individual stream.
requirements.required_behavior: Use Stream Identifier 0x00.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use Stream Identifier 0x00 for a frame associated with an individual stream.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame's semantic scope can be compared with its encoded Stream Identifier.

requirements.quote:
The structure and content of the frame payload are dependent entirely
   on the frame type.
requirements.condition: A frame payload is encoded or parsed.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the payload structure and content defined for the frame's Type.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload layout can be validated against the selected frame type.

requirements.quote:
The size of a frame payload is limited by the maximum size that a
   receiver advertises in the SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE setting.
requirements.condition: An endpoint sends a frame to a receiver that has advertised SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the frame payload at or below the advertised maximum size.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send a frame payload larger than the receiver's advertised SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound payload sizes can be compared directly with the peer's advertised value.

requirements.quote:
receiver advertises in the SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE setting.  This
   setting can have any value between 2^14 (16,384) and 2^24-1
   (16,777,215) octets, inclusive.
requirements.condition: A SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE value is produced or accepted.
requirements.required_behavior: Constrain the value to the inclusive range 16,384 through 16,777,215 octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use a SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE value below 16,384 or above 16,777,215.
requirements.why_checkable: The numeric setting value can be range-checked.

requirements.quote:
All implementations MUST be capable of receiving and minimally
   processing frames up to 2^14 octets in length, plus the 9-octet frame
   header (Section 4.1).  The size of the frame header is not included
   when describing frame sizes.
requirements.condition: An implementation receives a frame with a payload length of at most 16,384 octets and a 9-octet header.
requirements.required_behavior: Be capable of receiving and minimally processing the frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary-sized frames can be delivered and successful minimal processing observed.

requirements.quote:
All implementations MUST be capable of receiving and minimally
   processing frames up to 2^14 octets in length, plus the 9-octet frame
   header (Section 4.1).  The size of the frame header is not included
   when describing frame sizes.
requirements.condition: An implementation describes or enforces an HTTP/2 frame-size limit.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the described frame size as payload size and account for the 9-octet header separately.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include the 9-octet header in the described payload frame size.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary handling can be tested with a 16,384-octet payload plus its separate 9-octet header.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST send an error code of FRAME_SIZE_ERROR if a frame
   exceeds the size defined in SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE, exceeds any
   limit defined for the frame type, or is too small to contain
   mandatory frame data.  A frame size error in a frame that could alter
requirements.condition: A received frame exceeds the size defined in SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE.
requirements.error_behavior: Send an error code of FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: An oversized frame can be injected and the emitted error code observed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST send an error code of FRAME_SIZE_ERROR if a frame
   exceeds the size defined in SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE, exceeds any
   limit defined for the frame type, or is too small to contain
   mandatory frame data.  A frame size error in a frame that could alter
requirements.condition: A received frame exceeds a size limit defined for its frame type.
requirements.error_behavior: Send an error code of FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A frame violating its type-specific size limit can be injected and the emitted error code observed.

requirements.quote:
An endpoint MUST send an error code of FRAME_SIZE_ERROR if a frame
   exceeds the size defined in SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE, exceeds any
   limit defined for the frame type, or is too small to contain
   mandatory frame data.  A frame size error in a frame that could alter
requirements.condition: A received frame is too small to contain its mandatory frame data.
requirements.error_behavior: Send an error code of FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: An undersized frame can be injected and the emitted error code observed.

requirements.quote:
mandatory frame data.  A frame size error in a frame that could alter
   the state of the entire connection MUST be treated as a connection
   error (Section 5.4.1); this includes any frame carrying a field block
   (Section 4.3) (that is, HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, and CONTINUATION), a
   SETTINGS frame, and any frame with a stream identifier of 0.
requirements.condition: A frame-size error occurs in a frame that could alter the state of the entire connection.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame-size error as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: The error scope can be observed when a connection-state-affecting frame has an invalid size.

requirements.quote:
error (Section 5.4.1); this includes any frame carrying a field block
   (Section 4.3) (that is, HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, and CONTINUATION), a
   SETTINGS frame, and any frame with a stream identifier of 0.
requirements.condition: A frame-size error occurs in a HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, or CONTINUATION frame carrying a field block.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame-size error as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: The listed frame types can each be sent with an invalid size and the connection-level response observed.

requirements.quote:
error (Section 5.4.1); this includes any frame carrying a field block
   (Section 4.3) (that is, HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, and CONTINUATION), a
   SETTINGS frame, and any frame with a stream identifier of 0.
requirements.condition: A frame-size error occurs in a SETTINGS frame.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame-size error as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: An incorrectly sized SETTINGS frame can be injected and connection-level error handling observed.

requirements.quote:
error (Section 5.4.1); this includes any frame carrying a field block
   (Section 4.3) (that is, HEADERS, PUSH_PROMISE, and CONTINUATION), a
   SETTINGS frame, and any frame with a stream identifier of 0.
requirements.condition: A frame-size error occurs in a frame whose Stream Identifier is 0.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame-size error as a connection error.
requirements.why_checkable: An incorrectly sized stream-zero frame can be injected and connection-level error handling observed.

requirements.quote:
Each field block carries all of the compressed field lines of a
   single field section.  Header sections also include control data
   associated with the message in the form of pseudo-header fields
   (Section 8.3) that use the same format as a field line.
requirements.condition: A field block is constructed or decoded.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry all compressed field lines of exactly one field section in the field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Split one field section's compressed field lines across independent field blocks or combine multiple field sections in one field block.
requirements.why_checkable: Decoded field-block membership can be compared with field-section boundaries.

requirements.quote:
Each field block carries all of the compressed field lines of a
   single field section.  Header sections also include control data
   associated with the message in the form of pseudo-header fields
   (Section 8.3) that use the same format as a field line.
requirements.condition: A header section contains message-associated control data.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent that control data as pseudo-header fields using the same format as a field line.
requirements.why_checkable: The decoded header section can be inspected for the prescribed pseudo-header representation and format.

requirements.quote:
Field blocks carry control data and header sections for requests,
   responses, promised requests, and pushed responses (see Section 8.4).
requirements.condition: Control data or a header section is encoded for a request, response, promised request, or pushed response.
requirements.required_behavior: Carry the data in a field block.
requirements.why_checkable: Message encodings can be inspected to verify that their control data and header sections are carried in field blocks.

requirements.quote:
All these messages, except for interim responses and requests
   contained in PUSH_PROMISE (Section 6.6) frames, can optionally
   include a field block that carries a trailer section.
requirements.condition: A request, response, promised request, or pushed response is neither an interim response nor a request contained in a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.required_behavior: The message is permitted to include a field block carrying a trailer section.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's accepted and produced message forms can be tested for optional trailer field blocks.

requirements.quote:
All these messages, except for interim responses and requests
   contained in PUSH_PROMISE (Section 6.6) frames, can optionally
   include a field block that carries a trailer section.
requirements.condition: The message is an interim response or a request contained in a PUSH_PROMISE frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Include a field block carrying a trailer section.
requirements.why_checkable: Interim responses and PUSH_PROMISE-contained requests can be inspected for trailer field blocks; the exclusion directly identifies message forms outside the stated trailer permission.
